trigger.symptom: Threading alone gave no speed-up at D~99 (hpc_stan_exclusive_node.json).
trigger.cause: Hypothesis (since retracted as unsupported): reduce_sum deep-copies shared arguments that contain parameters, so slicing the parameters and sharing only data would remove the bottleneck. Launched threaded.

deviations.two_variables_changed: This launch changed BOTH the reduce_sum slicing and the thread count, so its negative signal could not be attributed to either. Relaunched with one variable in hpc_stan_reslice_serial.json.
deviations.cancel_cause_as_stated_at_the_time: The resliced threaded D~29 run had not reached about 100 iterations in 18 minutes while the pre-reslice run reached about 103 in about 5 minutes.
deviations.source: Slurm facts (state, elapsed, node, CPUs, submit time) come from sacct as read on 2026-10-13; cohort, host and W&B run id come from each run's W&B config. The two agree on node and duration for every job. sacct truncates the cancelling uid, so who issued each scancel is not recoverable from it; the causes below are the reasons stated at the time and are marked where they were later found wrong.

cost.progress_discarded: about 21 minutes of two large allocations
